title: Relative Phase and Rotations
summary: Z, S, T and Rz gates: same probabilities, different states.
mission: The circuit already prepares |+⟩. Rotate the vector a quarter turn around the Z axis, to the +Y point of the equator: the state (|0⟩ + i|1⟩)/√2.
hints: Rotations around Z move the vector along the equator without changing the probabilities. Try qc.z(0) and see where the vector ends up.
Z is a half turn (180°). You need a quarter turn (90°): the S gate, or qc.rz(theta, 0) with the right angle.
Add qc.s(0) after the Hadamard. With rz, import math and use qc.rz(math.pi / 2, 0).

prediction.question: The qubit is in |+⟩, with a 50% chance for each outcome. You apply the Z gate. What happens to the probabilities of measuring 0 and 1?
prediction.explanation: The Z gate only flips the sign of the |1⟩ amplitude. The magnitudes do not change, so the probabilities do not either. What changes is the relative phase: the vector goes to the opposite side of the equator.
